newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria seeks longer EBRD energy loan term.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria seeks longer EBRD energy loan term.

text.p: Bulgaria is seeking to extend the term of a 40 million Ecu ($44.6 million) loan from the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development for a sulphur reduction installation at a thermal power plant, a government spokeswoman said on Thursday.
Bulgaria signed an agreement with the EBRD in 1992 for a loan to help complete unit number eight at the Maritza East Two power complex in southern Bulgaria.
The term of the loan expired on June 30 and Bulgaria needs to extend it to the end of 1999 as only 36.6 percent of the total has been used so far, the spokeswoman said.
Thursday's cabinet meeting authorised the finance minister and national electricity company chief to sign an agreement with the bank for the extension.
Environmental officials say lignite from Maritsa East, which is the country's biggest mining and thermal power complex, has one of the highest sulphur contents in Europe.

Maritsa East, which meets 30 percent of the country's power demand, has reserves of some two billion tonnes which are expected to feed the country's coal-fired power stations for another 80 to 100 years.
-- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-91188 ($ = 0.896 European Currency Unit ECUs)
